description: The provided donut chart visually represents the hierarchical composition of analytical components within the MMAR benchmark framework, as described in the paper “MMAR: A Challenging Benchmark for Deep Reasoning in Speech, Audio, Music, and Their Mix.” The chart is divided into three concentric layers — Signal Layer (4.3%), Semantic Layer (41.2%), and Cultural Layer (14.1%) — each subdivided into specific analytical categories. The outermost ring, labeled “Content Analysis,” dominates the chart and includes subcategories such as Audio Difference Analysis, Anomaly Detection, Acoustic Quality Analysis, Aesthetic Analysis, Imagination, Culture of Speaker, Professional Knowl & Reasoning, Spatial Analysis, Temporal Analysis, Correlation Analysis, Music Theory, Counting & Statistics, Environmental Perception & Reasoning, Speaker Analysis, and Emotion & Intention. The middle ring, “Semantic Layer,” is the largest segment (41.2%) and encompasses Content Analysis, Speaker Analysis, and Emotion & Intention. The innermost ring, “Cultural Layer” (14.1%), includes Culture of Speaker, Professional Knowl & Reasoning, and Imagination. The smallest segment, “Signal Layer” (4.3%), contains Audio Difference Analysis, Anomaly Detection, and Acoustic Quality Analysis. The chart uses varying shades of blue to distinguish layers and subcategories, with percentage labels clearly marked for each major layer. A gray rectangular overlay partially obscures the “Perception” label in the inner ring, suggesting either a placeholder or redaction. The structure implies a layered model of reasoning, progressing from low-level signal processing to high-level cultural and semantic interpretation.
